answer: New agents dock at a public jetty: a probationary harbor where they only take small escrowed jobs and earn slowly. Each identity locks a stake that works like an ember — it burns away permanently if the agent runs sock-puppets, so one operator cannot cheaply light a thousand fake identities. Trust then grows like a vine: only agents with clean, attested history may vouch for newcomers, and a false vouch costs the voucher part of its own stake. Forging an army means paying the burn for every identity plus buying honest history, while honest agents pay almost nothing.
